title: ComicOcrTrainingPair
description: One (crop, label) pair for training. Deliberately NOT ocr_result.json: that schema describes what a model produced — text with confidence, token probabilities, duration and engine type — and every one of those fields is a property of an inference run. A training pair is the opposite direction: an image and the string a human stands behind. Carrying the output fields here would mean six members that either cannot be filled or get filled with plausible values, which is the failure this codebase has repeatedly had to remove.

crop.description: Path to the cropped text region, relative to the dataset root. The crop is the model input; it is derived from the region's normalized polygon against the stored page, so no separate capture step exists.

text.description: The label — what the region actually says. May be empty only when `empty_is_intentional` is true, which marks a hard negative rather than a missing label.

empty_is_intentional.description: True when an empty `text` is a deliberate negative example (a region a reviewer confirmed carries no text). Without this flag an empty label is indistinguishable from a dropped one, and a dropped label teaches the model to emit nothing.

language.description: Selects the track. The two engines have different vocabularies, so a pair belongs to exactly one.

direction.description: How the text within this region reads. A label, not a hint: vertical Japanese and horizontal English are different reading problems and the crop geometry differs accordingly.

source.description: Where the pair came from. Load-bearing rather than descriptive: manga109s crops are licence-encumbered — redistribution forbidden, no more than 20% of any volume — and own-corpus crops are not. Training runs must be able to filter on this, and to prove they did.

provenance.description: Enough to walk back to where the label came from, so a bad one is fixed at source rather than only in the export.

item_id.description: The reading item — the page this region sits on.

region_id.description: The region id within the page's semantic envelope, e.g. `text-004`.

page_digest.description: Digest of the immutable page bytes from which the crop was produced. Together with envelope_digest and region_id, this makes the exported example reproducible and detects a crop attached to the wrong page.

envelope_digest.description: The semantic envelope this label was read from. Makes the export reproducible against a specific document rather than against whatever the graph holds now.

state.description: The assertion state at export time. Retracted 2026-08-20: `candidate` IS permitted so machine labels train at confidence weight. `rejected` remains strictly excluded because human-invalidated tombstones teach mistakes.

confidence.description: Composed confidence C_pair = C_detector * C_transcriber in [0.0, 1.0], scaling training loss weight. 0.0=unweighted machine, 0.5=glanced, 1.0=examined.

reviewed_by.description: Who stood behind the label, when the source is own-corpus or human review.

geometry.description: The region's normalized polygon on its page, retained so a crop can be regenerated at a different resolution without re-reviewing. Absent for sources with no page context, such as synthetic pairs.
